about: How the synthetic Guarani voice (facebook/mms-tts-grn, tools/make-tts.py) is given the words that are not Guarani spelling: Spanish names, numbers and loans inside Guarani lines. For the synthesis text only: the screens and the manifest keep the course's spelling. The voice reads letters the Guarani way (c before i as «ch» or «k»; a word without a written mark with the stress on its last vowel), so a Spanish word is written here as a Guarani speaker would spell what is said: h for the jota, k for c and qu, s for c and z, and the acute on the stressed vowel when it is not the last (two names take a nasal vowel there instead, because with the acute their n came back m: Ana → ãna, Ramona → ramõna). 'words': the course's word in lower case → what the voice is given, and why. 'as_written': the start of names that are Guarani spelling and are said as written, with any suffix (Itauguápe). 'spanish': the Spanish number words. A line of the Guarani voices made of these words alone is said by the Spanish voice, unshifted, when one of its words is marked "voice": "es" below (the Guarani voice cannot say it) or has no entry at all (it was never tried); a number the Guarani voice says right stays with it. A word that is not here and is not Guarani spelling stops tools/make-tts.py, with its key. The spellings are sound; what the voice then says is another matter: it has no f, no dependable l (it fails at the start of a word, between vowels and at the end), no ld, rl, tr, rt, dr, rm, rn, st or kt, no d without n and no last r, and no respelling repairs that (sound/VOICE.md, «How the text is prepared»). The people of the course whose names had one of these were given other names on 2026-11-10 (sound/VOICE.md, «The names of the people»); a new name goes through the same trial before a lesson uses it. Every entry was said three times or more and sent through two speech recognisers, in the first round, in the verification (three seeds each inside «che réra …»), in the fix round or in the names trial of 2026-11-10 (inside «che réra …», opening a sentence, closing one and after «héra …»; six seeds each for the names in use); none was heard by a person.

juan.why: The Spanish jota. After «che réra» the model says the name with an h by itself, but after «mba'éichapa» it came back «joan»; with h it is the same every time. Heard right by the large recogniser 3 times of 3. In the names trial of 2026-11-10: inside «che réra …», closing a sentence and after «héra …», right in 13 takes of 18 for the independent recogniser and 18 of 18 for the large one; opening a sentence («huan oho ko ka'aru»), in none of 6 for either («voan», «po'an», «koan»): the h that opens an utterance is lost. No recorded line opens with Juan today, and none should.

josé.why: The Spanish jota; the last vowel is stressed without a mark. Heard right 3 times of 3, and in the names trial of 2026-11-10 in 22 takes of 24 by each recogniser.

jose.why: The same name written without its accent.

ramona.why: The stress is on the o, written for the voice with a nasal õ, not with an acute. With the acute, «ramóna», the n came back m for both recognisers («ramoma» in 23 hearings of 48): right in 8 takes of 24 for the independent one and 12 of 24 for the large one, and in none of 6 after «héra». The voice says a nasal vowel higher, which marks the stress, and a vowel before n is nasal in speech anyway: as «ramõna» the name is heard right in 19 takes of 24 and 22 of 24 (the names trial of 2026-11-10: inside «che réra …», opening and closing a sentence, after «héra …»); opening a sentence the r is weak either way («amona», «pamona»). In M's voice, 5 takes of 9 and 7 of 9. Without any mark, «ramona», 9 and 10 takes of 12, the stress unmarked. For a native ear: does «ramõna» sound like the name?

rosa.why: The stress is on the o. With the acute the recognisers write «rósa» in 8 hearings of 12; without it, in none. The r is the soft Guarani r, not the strong first r of Spanish. Heard right 3 times of 3, and in the names trial of 2026-11-10 in 21 takes of 24 and 23 of 24.

ana.why: The stress is on the first a, written for the voice with a nasal ã, not with an acute. As «ána» the n came back m or was lost («ama» in 8 hearings of 48, «aga», «anda»): right in 15 takes of 24 for the independent recogniser and 20 of 24 for the large one, and in M's voice in 4 of 9 and 7 of 9. As «ãna» the name is heard right in 22 takes of 24 and 23 of 24, and in M's voice in 7 of 9 and 8 of 9 (the names trial of 2026-11-10). The voice says a nasal vowel higher, which marks the stress, and the a before n is nasal in speech anyway. For a native ear: does «ãna» sound like the name?

tomás.why: As written; listed because it ends in a consonant. Heard right 3 times of 3, and in the names trial of 2026-11-10 in 24 takes of 24 by each recogniser.

tomas.why: The same name written without its accent.

vicente.why: c before e is s; the stress is on the second e. Tried on 2026-11-10 inside «che réra …», opening «… oho ko ka'aru», closing «mba'éichapa reiko …» and after «héra …»: heard with the right letters by the independent recogniser in 20 takes of 24 and by the large one in 22 of 24 (when not: «misente», «risente», «guisente»). At the start of a sentence the v is weak in one take of three («misente», «guisente»). In M's voice, 6 takes of 9 and 9 of 9; the Spanish voice says the name right 3 times of 3.

moisés.why: As written: the stress is on the last vowel and marked already; listed because it ends in a consonant. Tried on 2026-11-10 inside «che réra …», opening «… oho ko ka'aru», closing «mba'éichapa reiko …» and after «héra …»: heard with the right letters by the independent recogniser in 16 takes of 24 and by the large one in 24 of 24 (when not: «moise», «moikseiks», «moiseks»). The last s is weak for the independent recogniser at the end of an utterance («moise» in 3 takes of 6 of «che réra moisés»). In M's voice, 6 takes of 9 and 9 of 9; the Spanish voice, 3 of 3.

moises.why: The same name written without its accent.

santiago.why: The stress is on the a. Tried on 2026-11-10 inside «che réra …», opening «… oho ko ka'aru», closing «mba'éichapa reiko …» and after «héra …»: heard with the right letters by the independent recogniser in 19 takes of 24 and by the large one in 24 of 24 (when not: «sanqiago», «santiagvo», «santiaago»). In M's voice (2 semitones lower) the independent recogniser hears «santiavo», «santiagu» in 9 takes of 9 and the large one «santiago» in 9 of 9: no line of M says the name today.

casimiro.why: c before a is k; the stress is on the second i. Tried on 2026-11-10 inside «che réra …», opening «… oho ko ka'aru», closing «mba'éichapa reiko …» and after «héra …»: heard with the right letters by the independent recogniser in 19 takes of 24 and by the large one in 20 of 24 (when not: «kasimire», «kasimbro», «kasimivo»). In M's voice the r is weak («kasimio»): 5 takes of 9 each.

genaro.why: g before e is the jota: h. The stress is on the a. Tried on 2026-11-10 inside «che réra …», opening «… oho ko ka'aru», closing «mba'éichapa reiko …» and after «héra …»: heard with the right letters by the independent recogniser in 17 takes of 24 and by the large one in 19 of 24 (when not: «henar», «henalo», «henalva»). The o is swallowed before a word that begins with o («henar oho»: 5 hearings). In M's voice, «maitei henáro» is heard right 3 times of 3 by both.

tito.why: The stress is on the i. Tried on 2026-11-10 inside «che réra …», opening «… oho ko ka'aru», closing «mba'éichapa reiko …» and after «héra …»: heard with the right letters by the independent recogniser in 19 takes of 24 and by the large one in 21 of 24 (when not: «tita», «tiko»). After a word that ends in o the last vowel came back a («tita») in 7 hearings.

jacinto.why: The Spanish jota is h and c before i is s; the stress is on the i. Tried on 2026-11-10 inside «che réra …», opening «… oho ko ka'aru», closing «mba'éichapa reiko …» and after «héra …»: heard with the right letters by the independent recogniser in 23 takes of 24 and by the large one in 24 of 24 (when not: «hasindo»). In M's voice, 9 takes of 9 each; the Spanish voice, after «qué responde», 1 take of 3 («rasinto»).

sara.why: The stress is on the first a. Tried on 2026-11-10 inside «che réra …», opening «… oho ko ka'aru», closing «mba'éichapa reiko …» and after «héra …»: heard with the right letters by the independent recogniser in 17 takes of 24 and by the large one in 24 of 24 (when not: «ssara», «chara»). At the start of a sentence the independent recogniser writes «ssara» (6 takes of 6): a long first s, not another letter.

teresa.why: The stress is on the second e. Tried on 2026-11-10 inside «che réra …», opening «… oho ko ka'aru», closing «mba'éichapa reiko …» and after «héra …»: heard with the right letters by the independent recogniser in 21 takes of 24 and by the large one in 24 of 24 (when not: «tersa»). After «héra» the independent recogniser hears «tersa» in 3 takes of 6.

karina.why: The stress is on the i. Tried on 2026-11-10 inside «che réra …», opening «… oho ko ka'aru», closing «mba'éichapa reiko …» and after «héra …»: heard with the right letters by the independent recogniser in 20 takes of 24 and by the large one in 21 of 24 (when not: «kaina», «harina», «kar'ina»). At the start of a sentence, «kaina» and «harina» in 3 takes of 6 for each recogniser.

tania.why: The stress is on the first a. Tried on 2026-11-10 inside «che réra …», opening «… oho ko ka'aru», closing «mba'éichapa reiko …» and after «héra …», three seeds each: heard with the right letters by the independent recogniser in 10 takes of 12 and by the large one in 11 of 12. Chosen by the lead for Ana's daughter in place of Jimena (said «hiména», one sound from iména, «su marido») and of Tamara (too like Tomás and Samanta, the children of the same unit); no clip says it today.

samanta.why: The stress is on the second a. Tried on 2026-11-10 inside «che réra …», opening «… oho ko ka'aru», closing «mba'éichapa reiko …» and after «héra …»: heard with the right letters by the independent recogniser in 23 takes of 24 and by the large one in 24 of 24 (when not: «ssamanta»).

susana.why: The stress is on the a. Tried on 2026-11-10 inside «che réra …», opening «… oho ko ka'aru», closing «mba'éichapa reiko …» and after «héra …»: heard with the right letters by the independent recogniser in 22 takes of 24 and by the large one in 24 of 24 (when not: «susna», «susaga»). In M's voice the independent recogniser hears «chusana» in 3 takes of 9 (the large one is right in 9 of 9).

maría.why: As written: the stress is marked already. Tried on 2026-11-10 inside «che réra …», opening «… oho ko ka'aru», closing «mba'éichapa reiko …» and after «héra …»: heard with the right letters by the independent recogniser in 13 takes of 24 and by the large one in 17 of 24 (when not: «marie», «mariae», «marive»). The last two vowels come back «ie» or «iae» in 14 hearings of 48 («marie», «mariae»): the weakest of the names in use. Without the acute, «maria», the letters are heard right in 11 and 10 takes of 12, but the stress is then unmarked; with a nasal ĩ, «marĩa», no better (13 and 19 of 24).

maria.why: The same name written without its accent.

luque.why: qu is k, and the stress is on the u. NOT RENDERED: the l that opens the word («ndúke», «núke» in 6 hearings of 6).

argentina.why: g before e is the jota: h. The stress is on the i. The r before the h is lost, as in Argentina-gua.

argentina-gua.why: The place name with -gua, as one word: h for the jota, no hyphen (the model has a hyphen that makes no sound of its own), and no acute, because -gua takes the stress. The r is lost: «ahentinagua» from both recognisers.

diez.why: z is s. Only for a number inside a Guarani sentence: a line that is nothing but a Spanish number with this word in it goes to the Spanish voice (see 'spanish'), because the Guarani voice has no d without n and drops a last l: «diez mil» came back garbled («riesmi», «ndiehmi», «liémi») in each of the eight spellings tried.

mil.why: As written; listed because it ends in a consonant. The last l is not said: the two recognisers heard «mi» in 5 hearings of 6, «miĩ» in the other.

veinte.why: The stress is on the e. Came back «véinte» from both recognisers in 6 takes of 6, and from the large one 3 times of 3 in the verification.

treinta.why: The stress is on the e. NOT RENDERED: the cluster tr. Alone, as «tréinta», it came back «téinta» from the independent recogniser 6 times of 6 and «ténta» or «téinta» from the large one in 4 of 6; without the acute, «tereinta» (6 of 6). So a line that is only this number goes to the Spanish voice («treinta» in 2 takes of 3); inside a Guarani sentence it is said «tréinta», flawed.

cuarenta.why: c is k; the stress is on the e. Alone it came back «kuarénta» from the independent recogniser in 5 takes of 6 and «cuarenta», «kuarenta» from the large one in 6 of 6; inside «oguereko … ary», «kuarénta» 3 times of 3 (independent).

cincuenta.why: c is s and k; the stress is on the e. NOT RENDERED: the n before k («cikenta», «si cuenta» in 10 hearings of 12). A line that is only this number goes to the Spanish voice («cincuenta» 3 times of 3).

sesenta.why: The stress is on the second e. Said alone by F the first s is lost for the large recogniser («esen a» twice, nothing once), though M's take is heard right 3 times of 3: not dependable, so a line that is only this number goes to the Spanish voice («sesenta» 3 of 3).

setenta.why: The stress is on the second e. As sesenta: said alone by F it came back «etenta» from the large recogniser 3 times of 3; the Spanish voice says «setenta» 3 of 3.

noventa.why: The stress is on the e. Alone it came back «novénta» from the independent recogniser and «noventa» from the large one in 6 takes of 6 each; inside «oguereko … ary», «novénta» in 2 takes of 3.

cien.why: c is s. Alone it came back «csien», «cshien», «cén», «sén»: right in 2 hearings of 12. A line that is only this number goes to the Spanish voice («cien» 3 of 3).

doce.why: c before e is s; the stress is on the o. NOT RENDERED: the d («ndose», «ndosẽ» in 15 hearings of 18: a bare d comes out as the Guarani nd). A line that is only this number goes to the Spanish voice («doce» 3 of 3); inside a Guarani sentence it is said «dóse», flawed.

ochenta.why: The stress is on the e. Alone it came back «ochénta» or «ochenta» in 6 hearings of 6 by F; in M's voice the large recogniser heard «osénta» twice in 3. The ch is the Guarani one, «sh»; after a word that ends in o the first o is swallowed («oguereko chénta»).
